- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If model shows early downward correction after a spike, but true outcome continues rising, delay downward adjustment until at least 3–5 days after peak.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts a sharp drop, often overshoots — cap downward forecasts at 10–15% below recent low if sentiment remains negative.
- Model frequently underestimates late-period rallies (last 7–10 days of forecast) — increase final 5–7 days’ forecast by 2–5% if sentiment turns positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend if sentiment shifts direction.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to 1.00 but price doesn’t follow, reduce forecast sensitivity by 20–30% for next 3 days.
